L01-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.051 and licensing standards, proper lane positioning requires maintaining the vehicle squarely centered within the marked travel lane, without crowding oncoming traffic or drifting onto roadway shoulders.

L01-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: Texas DPS examiners grade applicants on four designated basic skills (COPS): Control (steering & vehicle handling), Observation (traffic scanning), Positioning (lane placement), and Signaling (communicating intent).

L01-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: The Texas Driver Handbook establishes the 'three-second rule' for safe following distance under good weather. Count three seconds after the lead vehicle passes a fixed landmark before your vehicle reaches it.

L01-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §545.351 (Basic Speed Rule) mandates that an operator may not drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under prevailing conditions, regardless of maximum posted limits.

L01-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §548.051 and DPS inspection regulations, passenger vehicle tires must have a minimum tread depth of at least 2/32 inch in all major grooves to pass annual safety inspection.

L01-T02-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.151, at an all-way stop intersection, the vehicle that arrives first and comes to a complete stop has the right-of-way to proceed first.

L01-T02-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas MUTCD guidelines, yellow diamond signs serve as warning signs alerting drivers to upcoming hazards, merging traffic, or physical roadway changes requiring caution.

L01-T02-Q3.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §601.072 establishes mandatory 30/60/25 minimum coverage: $30,000 for injury/death of one person, $60,000 for two or more persons in a single crash, and $25,000 for property damage.

L01-T02-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §544.008, a flashing red signal functions legally as a stop sign. Drivers must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk/intersection, yielding right-of-way.

L01-T02-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §724.011, operating a motor vehicle on public roads constitutes implied consent to chemical breath or blood testing if lawfully arrested for suspected DWI.

L01-T03-Q1.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §545.157 requires drivers passing stationary emergency, tow, or highway vehicles with lights flashing to vacate the adjacent lane or slow 20 mph below posted limits (50 mph in a 70 zone).

L01-T03-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.066, drivers on a separate roadway separated by an intervening physical space or barrier (such as a raised median) are not required to stop for a school bus.

L01-T03-Q3.statutory_rationale: Texas law mandates that any child younger than 8 years old, unless they are at least 4 feet 9 inches tall, must be secured in an approved child passenger safety seat system.

L01-T03-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §550.021 & §550.023, failing to immediately stop, remain at the scene, render reasonable assistance (including medical aid), and provide identity info is a felony offense.

L01-T03-Q5.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §521.292 authorizes DPS to suspend the license of a 'habitual violator,' defined as having four or more moving traffic violation convictions in 12 months, or seven in 24 months.

L02-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §521.025 requires an operator to have their driver license in their possession while driving and display it upon the demand of a magistrate or peace officer.

L02-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §521.029, a new resident who is at least 16 years of age and has a valid out-of-state license must obtain a Texas driver license within 90 days of establishing residency.

L02-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §521.054 mandates that a licensee must notify the DPS of any change of address or name within 30 days of the change occurring.

L02-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: Restriction Code 'A' on a Texas driver license specifies that the operator must wear corrective lenses (glasses or contact lenses) while operating a motor vehicle.

L02-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §521.271, a standard Class C driver license issued to individuals between ages 18 and 84 expires eight years from the date of issuance on the licensee's birthday.

L02-T02-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §521.083, a standard Class C license authorizes driving passenger vehicles with a GVWR of less than 26,001 pounds towing a trailer not exceeding 10,000 pounds.

L02-T02-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §522.003, operating a single vehicle with a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) of 26,001 pounds or more requires a Commercial Driver License (CDL).

L02-T02-Q3.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §521.084 specifies that a Class M license is required to operate a motorcycle or moped on Texas public roads.

L02-T02-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §521.222, an instruction permit holder must be accompanied by a licensed driver at least 21 years old who has at least one year of driving experience, occupying the seat next to the driver.

L02-T02-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §521.223, DPS may issue a restricted hardship license to a minor who has completed driver education if failure to license would cause severe family economic or medical hardship.

L02-T03-Q1.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §521.341 mandates automatic driver license suspension upon conviction of DWI, Intoxication Assault, Intoxication Manslaughter, or evading arrest in a motor vehicle.

L02-T03-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §521.457, Driving While License Invalid (DWLI) with a prior conviction or without financial responsibility is a Class B misdemeanor punishable by up to 180 days in jail and a $2,000 fine.

L02-T03-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §521.242, an Occupational License permits an individual whose license is suspended to operate a non-commercial vehicle for essential work, school, or essential household chores.

L02-T03-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §521.313, a suspended driver cannot legally drive until paying the mandatory statutory reinstatement fee and providing proof of financial responsibility (SR-22).

L02-T03-Q5.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code Chapter 706 authorizes the DPS to deny driver license renewal to any individual who fails to appear in court or fails to pay valid traffic fines.

L02-T04-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §502.040 and the 'Two Steps, One Sticker' system, vehicles must pass a comprehensive state safety inspection within 90 days before vehicle registration can be renewed.

L02-T04-Q2.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §548.051 lists mandatory inspection items including service brakes, parking brake, steering mechanism, lighting, tires, horn, windshield wipers, and exhaust systems.

L02-T04-Q3.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §502.059 and TxDMV regulations require the registration insignia to be displayed in the lower left corner of the vehicle windshield.

L02-T04-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §504.943, passenger vehicles must display two license plates: one at the exterior front and one at the exterior rear, unobstructed and illuminated at night.

L02-T04-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §501.071 and §501.145, the purchaser of a used vehicle must submit title and registration paperwork within 30 days of sale to prevent financial penalties.

L02-T05-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §601.053, valid proof includes an insurance card, an insurance policy binder, a certificate of self-insurance, or a valid electronic digital image displayed on a phone.

L02-T05-Q2.statutory_rationale: TexasSure is an automated electronic verification program that checks insurance company databases to verify whether a vehicle has active liability coverage during traffic stops.

L02-T05-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §601.191, a first conviction for failure to maintain financial responsibility carries a fine of $175 to $350. Subsequent convictions carry fines up to $1,000.

L02-T05-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §601.151, if an uninsured driver causes a crash resulting in injury or damage of $1,000+, DPS suspends their license and registration unless they post cash security or settle damages.

L02-T05-Q5.statutory_rationale: An SR-22 is a certificate of financial responsibility filed by an insurance carrier directly with the Texas DPS, guaranteeing that the driver maintains mandatory coverage for a prescribed period.

L02-T06-Q1.statutory_rationale: Regular inspections ensure critical safety components (brakes, tires, lighting, wipers, steering) function properly, preventing unexpected mechanical failures that cause high-speed crashes.

L02-T06-Q2.statutory_rationale: A safe pre-drive walk-around involves checking tire inflation and wear, verifying clean and undamaged lights/mirrors, and scanning for children, pets, or obstacles around the vehicle perimeter.

L02-T06-Q3.statutory_rationale: Holding a driver license is a privilege carrying the duty to protect human life, obey traffic codes, and operate with courtesy and vigilance for all roadway participants.

L02-T06-Q4.statutory_rationale: Repeat traffic convictions lead to administrative license suspension under TTC §521.292, substantial auto insurance rate surges, and possible criminal prosecution for reckless driving.

L02-T06-Q5.statutory_rationale: In serious multi-vehicle crashes, medical treatment and modern vehicle replacement costs can easily exceed $30,000 per person or $60,000 per crash, exposing drivers to severe personal bankruptcy.

L02-T07-Q1.statutory_rationale: The program allows drivers with diagnosed communication impediments (autism, PTSD, deafness) to disclose their condition in state databases, preventing officer misunderstandings during stops.
L02-T07-Q1.statute: TEXAS GOVERNOR'S COMM. ON PEOPLE WITH DISABILITIES

L02-T07-Q2.statutory_rationale: When a plate is queried through the Texas Law Enforcement Telecommunications System (TLETS), the system displays a confidential notation alerting the officer before they approach the vehicle.

L02-T07-Q3.statutory_rationale: Qualifying diagnoses under Texas law include Autism Spectrum Disorder, speech and language disorders, deafness/hearing impairment, PTSD, Traumatic Brain Injury, and Down Syndrome.

L02-T07-Q4.statutory_rationale: DPS Form DL-101 must be completed and signed by a licensed physician or psychologist confirming the communication impediment diagnosis.

L02-T07-Q5.statutory_rationale: Form VTR-216 allows Texas motorists to request that their communication impediment be recorded in the TxDMV database, alerting law enforcement through TLETS.

L03-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas law, the law never gives anyone the right-of-way; it only states who must yield the right-of-way. Safe drivers yield whenever necessary to prevent a collision.

L03-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §545.151 states that at an intersection not controlled by an official device, the operator on the left must yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on their right.

L03-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.151, failing to yield causing a crash with serious bodily injury results in a fine of $1,000 to $4,000.

L03-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.155, an operator entering a highway from an alley, building, or private road must stop before the sidewalk and yield to all vehicles and pedestrians.

L03-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §552.003, drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks if the pedestrian is on the half of the roadway on which the vehicle is traveling or approaching closely.

L03-T02-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.152, an operator on an intersecting road that terminates must stop and yield to vehicles traveling on the through highway.

L03-T02-Q2.statutory_rationale: Texas Transportation Code §545.151 dictates that drivers on an unpaved roadway must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on a paved roadway.

L03-T02-Q3.statutory_rationale: In a roundabout, traffic already circulating inside has the right-of-way. Entering vehicles must yield and wait for a safe gap in the circular flow.

L03-T02-Q4.statutory_rationale: Drivers crossing divided highways must yield to the first roadway, move into the median opening if wide enough, and yield again to traffic on the second roadway.

L03-T02-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §544.008, when a signal flashes red in all directions, the intersection functions as an all-way stop. Drivers must stop completely and follow standard right-of-way rules.

L03-T03-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.152, an operator intending to turn left within an intersection must yield the right-of-way to oncoming vehicles approaching from the opposite direction.

L03-T03-Q2.statutory_rationale: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at opposing stop signs, the driver turning left across traffic must yield to the driver proceeding straight through or turning right.

L03-T03-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.153, a driver approaching a yield sign must slow down to a reasonable speed and yield the right-of-way, stopping completely if safety requires it.

L03-T03-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §544.007(d), unless a sign prohibits it, an operator may turn right on red only after coming to a complete stop and yielding to all pedestrians and approaching traffic.

L03-T03-Q5.statutory_rationale: Defensive driving teaches that it is never safe to demand the right-of-way. If another driver fails to yield, you must yield to avoid a crash—no one has the right-of-way if it causes an accident.

L03-T04-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.156, upon the approach of an authorized emergency vehicle with lights/siren, an operator must yield by immediately driving to the right-hand edge or curb and stopping.

L03-T04-Q2.statutory_rationale: Drivers must never stop inside an intersection. If an emergency vehicle approaches, proceed through the intersection first, then pull over to the right curb and stop.

L03-T04-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.066, passing a stopped school bus with active visual signals is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $500 to $1,250 for a first offense.

L03-T04-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas law, drivers must take all necessary precautions and come to a complete stop if necessary to avoid injuring a blind pedestrian guided by a service animal or using a white cane.

L03-T04-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.407, an operator may not follow closer than 500 feet behind a fire apparatus responding to a fire alarm, or drive into the block where it has stopped.

L03-T05-Q1.statutory_rationale: The Texas Move Over/Slow Down Act applies to stationary police, emergency medical, fire, tow trucks, TxDOT highway maintenance vehicles, and utility service vehicles with flashing lights.

L03-T05-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.157, if unable to vacate the adjacent lane, a driver must slow down to 20 mph below the posted speed limit (45 mph in a 65 mph zone).

L03-T05-Q3.statutory_rationale: If the posted speed limit is less than 25 mph, the driver must slow to 5 mph below the posted speed limit.

L03-T05-Q4.statutory_rationale: Violating the Move Over/Slow Down Act is punishable by a fine of $500 to $1,250, and up to $4,000 and jail time if the violation results in serious bodily injury.

L03-T05-Q5.statutory_rationale: Safe execution requires early scanning, activating the turn signal at least 100 feet in advance, checking mirrors and blind spots, and smoothly moving over without sudden swerving.

L03-T06-Q1.statutory_rationale: Right-of-way laws exist to provide a predictable, orderly system that eliminates ambiguity and prevents fatal collisions through mutual legal obligations to yield.

L03-T06-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.154, drivers entering an access-controlled highway from an access road must yield the right-of-way to vehicles on or exiting the highway.

L03-T06-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.251, when a signal indicates an approaching train, an operator must stop between 15 feet and 50 feet from the nearest rail.

L03-T06-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas law, lawful instructions from a designated construction flagger take precedence over existing signs and signals. Disobeying carries doubled fines.

L03-T06-Q5.statutory_rationale: In Texas, vehicles in a funeral procession with headlights on have right-of-way. Other motorists must not cut through or interfere with the procession.

L03-T07-Q1.statutory_rationale: Intersections account for over 50% of fatal and injury crashes in Texas, primarily because side-impact crashes leave occupants protected by only thin door panels.

L03-T07-Q2.statutory_rationale: Safe intersection crossing requires scanning left, center, right, and left again before entering, ensuring cross traffic is actually stopping regardless of signal color.

L03-T07-Q3.statutory_rationale: A defensive driver never engages in an intersection confrontation. Yielding the right-of-way prevents a high-speed collision and defuses potential road rage.

L03-T07-Q4.statutory_rationale: A 'stale green' is a light that has been green for a long time. Covering the brake allows prompt, smooth stopping if it turns yellow, preventing intersection crashes.

L03-T07-Q5.statutory_rationale: A yellow light warns that red is imminent. If you can stop safely before the stop line, you must stop. If you are past the point of no return, proceed with caution.

L04-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: MUTCD W8-5 warns drivers that the road surface ahead is especially slippery when wet. Drivers should reduce speed and avoid sudden braking or hard steering.

L04-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: A pentagon (house-shaped) sign is reserved exclusively for School Zones and School Crossings, warning motorists of school children and pedestrian activity.

L04-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: The MUTCD R5-1 'Do Not Enter' sign marks a one-way roadway or freeway ramp where vehicular entry is prohibited because oncoming traffic is traveling toward you.

L04-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: Orange signs are temporary traffic control warning signs for construction and maintenance work zones, where traffic fines double when workers are present.

L04-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.055, a solid double yellow centerline indicates a no-passing zone for traffic in both directions.

L04-T02-Q1.statutory_rationale: A steady yellow signal warns that the green movement is terminating and a red signal will immediately follow. Drivers should stop if safe to do so.

L04-T02-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §544.008(b), an illuminated flashing yellow signal requires an operator to proceed through the intersection or past the signal only with caution.

L04-T02-Q3.statutory_rationale: A green arrow signal indicates a protected turn. Oncoming traffic is stopped by a red light, allowing vehicles to turn safely in the direction of the arrow.

L04-T02-Q4.statutory_rationale: A steady red 'X' over a lane indicates that the lane is closed to traffic traveling in that direction. Drivers must not drive in or enter that lane.

L04-T02-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §544.004, drivers must obey all official traffic control devices unless otherwise directed by a police officer or emergency personnel.

L04-T03-Q1.statutory_rationale: Only TxDOT (on state highways) and local authorities (on streets under their jurisdiction) have legal authority to place official traffic-control devices.

L04-T03-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §544.006, placing unauthorized signs or signals that imitate official devices is a misdemeanor and a public nuisance subject to removal.

L04-T03-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas law, entering an intersection (crossing the stop line or crosswalk) after the light has turned red is an offense. If you entered on yellow, you may clear the intersection.

L04-T03-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Transportation Code §544.005 and Penal Code §28.03, damaging or tampering with a traffic control device is criminal mischief, punishable as a misdemeanor or felony.

L04-T03-Q5.statutory_rationale: In 2019, Texas enacted HB 1631 (TTC §707.020), prohibiting cities from operating red-light cameras, with very few grandfathered contracts that have now largely expired.

L04-T04-Q1.statutory_rationale: Advance warning signs provide preview time based on posted speed limits, giving drivers sufficient reaction time and stopping distance to adapt safely.

L04-T04-Q2.statutory_rationale: TTC §542.404 doubles traffic fines in maintenance or construction work zones when workers are present to protect road workers from fatal high-speed collisions.

L04-T04-Q3.statutory_rationale: Defensive driving requires scanning 12 to 15 seconds ahead (about a block in the city or a quarter-mile on highways) to identify hazards early and maintain escape paths.

L04-T04-Q4.statutory_rationale: An alert driver watches for geometric roadway cues (cross streets, crosswalk lines, stopped vehicles) and slows down to stop safely even if a sign is partially obstructed.

L04-T04-Q5.statutory_rationale: Work zones feature narrowed lanes, sudden barricades, drop-offs, loose gravel, and sudden lane shifts that make high-speed maneuvers hazardous.

L05-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: Optimal traffic flow is achieved when vehicles move at consistent, predictable speeds while preserving safe following buffers, preventing phantom braking shockwaves.

L05-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: Tailgating forces sudden braking; following cars brake harder, creating a backward-traveling shockwave that halts traffic miles behind the original driver.

L05-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: The Texas Driver Handbook establishes the three-second following interval as the safe minimum under ideal roadway and weather conditions.

L05-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.351 dictates that an operator may not drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under prevailing roadway conditions, regardless of posted limits.

L05-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.363, an operator may not drive so slowly as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic, unless reduced speed is necessary for safety.

L05-T02-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §542.501, a driver must comply with any lawful order or direction of a police officer, which legally supersedes electronic traffic signals.

L05-T02-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §544.008, a flashing circular red signal requires a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk, or intersection, identical to a standard stop sign.

L05-T02-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §544.008(b), an operator facing a flashing yellow signal may proceed through the intersection or past the signal only with caution.

L05-T02-Q4.statutory_rationale: Ramp meters regulate the frequency of vehicles entering the freeway, spacing out entering traffic so they merge seamlessly into freeway gaps without causing congestion.

L05-T02-Q5.statutory_rationale: A steady red 'X' over a reversible or managed lane means that lane is closed to approaching traffic, and operating in that lane is strictly prohibited.

L05-T03-Q1.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.104(b) explicitly mandates that an operator intending to turn a vehicle shall signal continuously for not less than the last 100 feet of travel before turning.

L05-T03-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.107, an arm signal to stop or suddenly decrease speed is given by extending the hand and arm downward from the vehicle's left side.

L05-T03-Q3.statutory_rationale: Four-way emergency hazard flashers are designed to warn other motorists of a vehicular traffic hazard, disabled vehicle, or unexpected road obstruction.

L05-T03-Q4.statutory_rationale: Signaling communicates intention, but never confers right-of-way. The merging driver must yield to vehicles already occupying the lane and move only when safe.

L05-T03-Q5.statutory_rationale: TTC §547.501 mandates that a motor vehicle horn shall emit a sound audible under normal conditions from a distance of at least 200 feet, used only for safety warnings.

L05-T04-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.057, passing on the right is permitted when the vehicle overtaken is making or about to make a left turn, without driving off the main traveled pavement.

L05-T04-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.302(b)(1), an operator may not stand or park a vehicle within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, ensuring emergency fire engines have unobstructed access.

L05-T04-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.302(b)(4), an operator may not park within 30 feet upon the approach to any flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign, or traffic-control signal.

L05-T04-Q4.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.406 prohibits coasting in neutral on a downgrade because engine braking is lost, resulting in rapid brake overheating and reduced emergency vehicle control.

L05-T04-Q5.statutory_rationale: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb (toward the street center) so that if brakes fail, the back of the front tire rolls against the curb and stops.

L05-T05-Q1.statutory_rationale: The rear blind spot of an 18-wheeler extends up to 200 feet behind the trailer. If you follow closely, the driver cannot see you and you lose forward sight distance.

L05-T05-Q2.statutory_rationale: BGE settings turn side mirrors outward approximately 15 degrees so cars leaving the center rearview mirror appear immediately in the side mirror, eliminating blind spots.

L05-T05-Q3.statutory_rationale: Mirrors cannot eliminate every blind angle, especially for narrow profiles like motorcycles or bicycles. A quick shoulder check confirms the adjacent space is clear.
L05-T05-Q3.statute: TX TRANS CODE §545.060 / TX DRIVER HANDBOOK CH. 6

L05-T05-Q4.statutory_rationale: Lingering in a blind spot deprives both drivers of an escape route. If the other driver swerves or changes lanes without looking, a side-swipe collision is inevitable.

L05-T05-Q5.statutory_rationale: Because the driver sits on the left, the right-side blind spot is substantially larger, extending across multiple lanes. Passing on the right of a truck is extremely hazardous.

L05-T06-Q1.statutory_rationale: Select a fixed overhead sign or pole. When the lead vehicle passes it, count 'one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three'. Your car should not pass the mark before three.

L05-T06-Q2.statutory_rationale: While 2 seconds is acceptable under 30 mph in city driving, speeds above 30 mph demand at least 4 seconds following interval, and 4 seconds is best practice for new drivers.

L05-T06-Q3.statutory_rationale: Motorcycles have excellent braking capabilities and can stop in much shorter distances than passenger cars. Following closely creates severe risk of running over the rider.

L05-T06-Q4.statutory_rationale: Average perception time (0.75s) plus reaction time (0.75s) totals approximately 1.5 seconds. At 50 mph, your car travels 109 feet during this 1.5 seconds before brakes even engage.

L05-T06-Q5.statutory_rationale: Maintain at least a full vehicle length behind a stopped motorcycle. If your vehicle is rear-ended from behind, this buffer prevents crushing the vulnerable rider.

L05-T07-Q1.statutory_rationale: Kinetic energy equals 1/2 m v^2. When speed doubles, kinetic energy increases by 2 squared (4 times). Therefore, it takes four times more distance to stop the car.

L05-T07-Q2.statutory_rationale: At 50 mph, driver reaction distance is approximately 109 feet (at 1.5s) and vehicle braking distance is 120 feet, totaling approximately 229 feet to stop completely.

L05-T07-Q3.statutory_rationale: TTC §547.612 and Texas safety inspection standards require at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. Tires below 2/32 inch cannot evacuate water and hydroplane easily.

L05-T07-Q4.statutory_rationale: Water reduces pavement coefficient of friction by 50% or more, doubling braking distance. Drivers must reduce speed and extend following distances accordingly.

L05-T07-Q5.statutory_rationale: With ABS, remember 'Stomp, Stay, and Steer': stomp hard on the pedal, hold firm continuous pressure despite pulsating sensations, and steer toward safety.

L05-T08-Q1.statutory_rationale: Just 6 inches of water stalls cars and can sweep pedestrians off their feet; 12 to 24 inches (1 to 2 feet) will float and carry away most passenger cars, SUVs, and trucks.

L05-T08-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §472.022, driving around a barricade erected for flooding is a Class B misdemeanor (fines up to $1,000 and/or jail up to 180 days, escalating if bodily injury occurs).

L05-T08-Q3.statutory_rationale: Hydroplaning occurs when water builds in front of tires faster than the tread can channel it away. It can begin at speeds as low as 35 mph, with complete loss of traction at 55 mph.

L05-T08-Q4.statutory_rationale: Do not slam on brakes or steer abruptly. Ease off the gas pedal to let the vehicle decelerate naturally until tires regain contact with the pavement surface.

L05-T08-Q5.statutory_rationale: During dry spells, oil, grease, and exhaust grime build up on the road. When light rain starts, it mixes with these residues to form an extremely slick emulsion before washing away.

L05-T09-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.352(b)(1), the statutory prima facie speed limit in an urban district is 30 miles per hour unless altered by municipal authority.

L05-T09-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.352(b)(2), the prima facie speed limit on an alley or adjacent to a public beach is 15 miles per hour to protect pedestrians and beachfront visitors.

L05-T09-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.352, the statutory speed limit is 70 mph on numbered highways outside urban areas. In 2011, Texas repealed lower nighttime speed limits, making daytime and night limits uniform.

L05-T09-Q4.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.353 authorizes TxDOT to post speed limits up to 85 mph on highways designed to accommodate that speed (e.g., portions of State Highway 130 toll road).

L05-T09-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.363, the Texas Transportation Commission or local authorities may declare a minimum speed limit when engineering studies show slow speeds impede normal traffic.

L05-T10-Q1.statutory_rationale: TTC §547.302 mandates lighted headlamps at nighttime (30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise) and whenever persons/vehicles are not discernable for 1,000 feet.

L05-T10-Q2.statutory_rationale: TTC §547.333(c)(1) mandates dimming high-beam headlamps whenever an operator approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet.

L05-T10-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §547.333(c)(2), an operator following another vehicle within 300 feet to the rear must use low-beam lighting to prevent blinding the lead driver via mirrors.

L05-T10-Q4.statutory_rationale: Parking lights are for parking only. Operating a moving vehicle with only parking lights illuminated when headlights are required violates Texas vehicle equipment law.

L05-T10-Q5.statutory_rationale: High beams project light upward into water droplets, reflecting light back into the driver's eyes. Low beams project light down toward the pavement surface, illuminating the lane.

L05-T11-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.154, an operator on an access or feeder ramp entering a freeway or controlled-access highway shall yield right-of-way to vehicles on the highway main lanes.

L05-T11-Q2.statutory_rationale: Use the ramp and acceleration lane to accelerate to the cruising speed of freeway traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge smoothly into an open gap.

L05-T11-Q3.statutory_rationale: By standard highway convention and safety rules, the exiting vehicle (leaving high-speed traffic) is given priority, while the entering vehicle yields and adjusts position.

L05-T11-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.415, backing on a controlled-access highway shoulder or roadway is illegal. Drivers who miss an exit must proceed to the next exit and safely double back.

L05-T11-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.051, when signed 'Left Lane For Passing Only', it is a traffic violation to cruise in the left lane; it may only be used for passing or making a left exit.

L05-T12-Q1.statutory_rationale: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy, trance-like state resulting from staring at monotonous unbroken road lines for long periods, severely dulling alertness and reaction time.

L05-T12-Q2.statutory_rationale: Take a 15-minute rest break every 2 hours or every 100 miles. Walk around, get fresh air, stretch muscles, and let your eyes rest from staring at highway lanes.

L05-T12-Q3.statutory_rationale: A microsleep lasts 3 to 5 seconds. At 65 mph, your vehicle travels roughly 100 feet per second—meaning you travel the length of an entire football field completely unconscious.

L05-T12-Q4.statutory_rationale: Sensory tricks mask sleepiness for only a few minutes. The brain remains severely sleep-deprived, and reaction times remain degraded. Real sleep is the only cure.

L05-T12-Q5.statutory_rationale: The human body circadian cycle experiences natural alertness dips between midnight and 6:00 AM, and a secondary circadian drop between 2:00 PM and 4:00 PM.

L05-T13-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.301, stopping on the main traveled portion of a highway is prohibited. Drivers must pull completely off the roadway onto the right shoulder.

L05-T13-Q2.statutory_rationale: Activate hazard lights, raise the hood, and tie a white cloth or paper to the driver door handle or antenna to indicate to DPS troopers and passing drivers that help is needed.

L05-T13-Q3.statutory_rationale: Standing on a highway shoulder is exceptionally hazardous; dozens of stranded motorists are struck and killed each year. The vehicle cabin and seatbelts offer structural protection.

L05-T13-Q4.statutory_rationale: Place one triangle 10 feet directly behind, a second 100 feet back on the shoulder, and a third 200 feet back (especially if approaching over a hill crest or curve).

L05-T13-Q5.statutory_rationale: Never work on the traffic side of a vehicle on a narrow shoulder. The risk of being clipped by passing vehicles is catastrophic. Call a tow truck or DPS for a lane cushion.

L05-T14-Q1.statutory_rationale: Take your foot off the gas and avoid sudden braking. Steer in the direction of the skid (if the rear slides right, steer right). As the car straightens, straighten wheels.

L05-T14-Q2.statutory_rationale: A blowout pulls hard toward the flat tire. Grip the wheel firmly with both hands, keep vehicle straight, ease off the accelerator, and brake gently only after control is stabilized.

L05-T14-Q3.statutory_rationale: Rapid pumping can build enough residual hydraulic pressure to stop. Simultaneously downshift to a lower gear to use engine braking, and apply parking brake gradually.

L05-T14-Q4.statutory_rationale: Jerking the wheel causes rollover or catapults the car into oncoming traffic. Hold straight, ease off the gas, slow to under 25 mph, check traffic, and ease back onto pavement.

L05-T14-Q5.statutory_rationale: Shift to neutral immediately. The engine will rev, but power to wheels is disconnected. Steer to the shoulder and brake safely. Turning off ignition could lock the steering wheel.

L05-T15-Q1.statutory_rationale: Unlike roadways insulated by ground soil, bridges are exposed to freezing air on all sides (top and bottom), causing moisture to turn into ice much earlier than normal roads.

L05-T15-Q2.statutory_rationale: Black ice is a thin sheet of transparent ice through which the dark road asphalt remains visible. Drivers mistake it for wet road and fail to reduce speed before losing control.

L05-T15-Q3.statutory_rationale: On ice and snow, stopping distances increase by up to 9 times. Expanding your following buffer to 6 to 10 seconds provides the necessary margin to react and stop without skidding.

L05-T15-Q4.statutory_rationale: On ice, if drive wheels slip, cruise control attempts to maintain speed by accelerating, which immediately breaks traction and sends the vehicle into an uncontrollable spin.

L05-T15-Q5.statutory_rationale: A winter roadside emergency kit should include blankets, warm clothes, flashlights, phone chargers, snacks, an ice scraper, and sand or cat litter for tire traction if stuck on ice.

L05-T16-Q1.statutory_rationale: A space cushion provides margin of safety. Having space on as many sides as possible gives you an escape route if a vehicle swerves or stops abruptly.

L05-T16-Q2.statutory_rationale: In heavy traffic, using both lanes until the merge point and taking turns (zipper merge) reduces speed differences between lanes and cuts queue lengths by up to 40%.

L05-T16-Q3.statutory_rationale: Looking 20 to 30 seconds ahead allows you to spot developing hazards, traffic backups, and lane blockages early, giving ample time to alter speed or lane without emergency maneuvers.

L05-T16-Q4.statutory_rationale: Never brake-check. Increase your following distance ahead so you will not need to brake suddenly, or change lanes safely when clear to encourage the tailgater to pass.

L05-T16-Q5.statutory_rationale: When drivers behave predictably—signaling intentions, maintaining steady speeds, and yielding by law—surrounding motorists can anticipate movements and avoid conflicts.

L05-T17-Q1.statutory_rationale: TTC §542.404 doubles traffic fines for moving violations committed in a construction or maintenance work zone when workers are present and appropriate warning signs are posted.

L05-T17-Q2.statutory_rationale: TTC §542.501 mandates that drivers comply with directions of designated flaggers in highway work zones. Flaggers protect workers and coordinate alternating one-lane traffic.

L05-T17-Q3.statutory_rationale: When regulatory work zone speed limit signs are posted, they are legally binding at all times unless accompanied by flashing lights or specific hour placards.

L05-T17-Q4.statutory_rationale: Work zones feature narrowed lanes, rough pavement, grooved asphalt, edge drop-offs, and unexpected detours requiring reduced speeds and total driver concentration.

L05-T17-Q5.statutory_rationale: Rear-end collisions caused by inattention, speeding, and tailgating are the most common work zone crashes. Drivers fail to notice stopped queues in time to halt.

L05-T18-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Health & Safety Code §365.012, disposing of litter under 5 pounds or less than 5 gallons is a Class C misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $500.

L05-T18-Q2.statutory_rationale: Dumping litter weighing between 5 lbs and 500 lbs (or 5 gallons to 100 cubic feet) is a Class B misdemeanor, punishable by a fine up to $2,000, up to 180 days in jail, or both.

L05-T18-Q3.statutory_rationale: TTC §725.021 mandates that an open truck or trailer carrying gravel, sand, trash, or loose materials must cover the load securely with a close-fitting canvas or tarp to prevent blowing.

L05-T18-Q4.statutory_rationale: Flying debris causes fatal multi-vehicle pileups when drivers swerve violently at high speed. Striking objects like tires, mattresses, or lumber punctures tires and breaks windshields.

L05-T18-Q5.statutory_rationale: Launched by TxDOT in 1986, 'Don't Mess with Texas' is an anti-litter campaign aimed at reducing highway trash, cutting cleanup costs, and protecting driver safety across the state.

L06-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: Texas Penal Code §49.01(2)(B) establishes 0.08 grams of alcohol per 100 mL of blood, 210 L of breath, or 67 mL of urine as the statutory per se intoxication threshold.

L06-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TPC §49.01(2)(A), intoxication also means not having the normal use of mental or physical faculties by reason of the introduction of alcohol, a drug, or any combination.

L06-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas law, having a legal prescription is not a defense to DWI. If any drug, medication, or combination impairs normal faculties, driving is strictly illegal.

L06-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: TPC §49.01(1) defines alcohol concentration as the number of grams of alcohol per 210 liters of breath, 100 milliliters of blood, or 67 milliliters of urine.

L06-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §522.101, commercial drivers are held to a stricter standard of 0.04 BAC. Driving a commercial vehicle with BAC of 0.04 or more results in commercial license disqualification.

L06-T02-Q1.statutory_rationale: The liver metabolizes about 90% of alcohol at an unchangeable rate of roughly one standard drink per hour (reducing BAC by approximately 0.015% per hour). Nothing speeds this up.

L06-T02-Q2.statutory_rationale: The synergistic effect occurs when two drugs (or alcohol plus medication) interact, producing impairment far greater than the sum of their individual effects (1 + 1 = 4 or more).

L06-T02-Q3.statutory_rationale: Judgment and self-control are the first faculties affected by alcohol. A driver loses the ability to recognize their own impairment and takes foolish risks long before speech slurs.

L06-T02-Q4.statutory_rationale: Coffee, cold showers, exercise, and heavy meals do not accelerate liver metabolism. The person remains just as drunk, merely wide awake. Only time eliminates alcohol.

L06-T02-Q5.statutory_rationale: Alcohol relaxes the eye muscles, causing blurred vision, narrowing peripheral vision into tunnel vision, destroying depth perception, and delaying pupil recovery after oncoming glare.

L06-T03-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TPC §49.04, a 1st DWI is a Class B misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $2,000, 72 hours to 180 days in jail (min 6 days if open container present), and license suspension.

L06-T03-Q2.statutory_rationale: TPC §49.045 makes driving while intoxicated with a passenger younger than 15 years old a State Jail Felony, carrying fines up to $10,000 and 180 days to 2 years in state jail.

L06-T03-Q3.statutory_rationale: TPC §49.07 defines Intoxication Assault (causing serious bodily injury to another while driving intoxicated) as a 3rd-degree felony punishable by 2 to 10 years in prison and up to $10,000 fine.

L06-T03-Q4.statutory_rationale: TPC §49.08 defines Intoxication Manslaughter (causing the death of another by accident or mistake while intoxicated) as a 2nd-degree felony (2 to 20 years in prison, fines up to $10,000).

L06-T03-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TPC §49.04(d), if an analysis shows an alcohol concentration of 0.15 or more, the offense is enhanced to a Class A misdemeanor (up to 1 year in jail and up to $4,000 fine).

L06-T04-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code §106.041, it is illegal for a minor (under 21) to operate a motor vehicle or watercraft with ANY detectable amount of alcohol in their system.

L06-T04-Q2.statutory_rationale: A 1st DUI by a Minor is a Class C misdemeanor punishable by up to $500 fine, 20 to 40 hours of alcohol-related community service, a 60-day license suspension, and alcohol awareness class.

L06-T04-Q3.statutory_rationale: A minor may only possess alcohol in the visible presence of an adult parent, guardian, or adult spouse, or in the scope of employment at a licensed establishment.

L06-T04-Q4.statutory_rationale: Attempting to purchase alcohol or using a fake ID is a Class C misdemeanor under TABC §106.02 / §106.07, carrying up to $500 fine, license suspension (30 days 1st offense), and community service.

L06-T04-Q5.statutory_rationale: Minors can be charged with full adult DWI under TPC §49.04 if their BAC is 0.08 or higher or they lost normal use of faculties, subjecting them to adult jail time and penalties.

L06-T05-Q1.statutory_rationale: TPC §49.031 defines an open container as a bottle, can, or other receptacle that contains any amount of alcoholic beverage and is open, has a broken seal, or the contents of which are partially removed.

L06-T05-Q2.statutory_rationale: Open containers may only be transported in a locked glove compartment, locked trunk, or behind the last upright seat in vehicles without a trunk (like hatchbacks or SUVs).

L06-T05-Q3.statutory_rationale: Knowingly possessing an open container in the passenger area of a motor vehicle on a public highway is a Class C misdemeanor, punishable by a fine up to $500.

L06-T05-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under TPC §49.04(c), if a person commits DWI and has an open container in their immediate possession, the minimum term of confinement increases from 72 hours to 6 continuous days in jail.

L06-T05-Q5.statutory_rationale: TPC §49.031 explicitly exempts passengers in buses, taxicabs, licensed limousines, and persons in the living quarters of a house trailer, motor home, or recreational vehicle.

L06-T06-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §724.011, by operating a motor vehicle on Texas public roads, a driver is deemed to have given consent to submit to the taking of specimens of breath or blood if arrested for DWI.

L06-T06-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §724.035, refusing to provide a breath or blood specimen results in an automatic 180-day driver license suspension for a first refusal (and 2 years for a subsequent refusal within 10 years).

L06-T06-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §524.022, if an adult driver submits to a chemical test and registers a BAC of 0.08 or more, their license is administratively suspended for 90 days on a first offense.

L06-T06-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §724.041, the driver has exactly 15 days from receiving the notice of suspension to request a hearing before an Administrative Law Judge. If not requested, suspension begins on day 40.

L06-T06-Q5.statutory_rationale: An Occupational Driver License (ODL / Essential Need License) under TTC §521.242 can be issued by a court allowing restricted driving for work, school, or essential household duties.

L06-T07-Q1.statutory_rationale: A designated driver is not the person who drank the least. A designated driver is someone who drinks ZERO alcohol and remains 100% sober to drive everyone home safely.

L06-T07-Q2.statutory_rationale: Impaired drivers exhibit drifting between lanes, straddling the centerline, abrupt panic stops, driving without lights at night, delayed reactions to green lights, and erratic speeds.

L06-T07-Q3.statutory_rationale: Stay far back to avoid collisions. Do not attempt to pass or intervene. Pull off the road safely or have a passenger call 911 with the vehicle description, location, and direction.

L06-T07-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code, adults who knowingly provide alcohol to minors or allow minors to drink on their property face criminal charges and severe civil wrongful death lawsuits.

L06-T07-Q5.statutory_rationale: Between attorney fees, court fines, bail, towing, license surcharges, increased insurance rates, and ignition interlock devices, a first-offense Texas DWI routinely costs $10,000 to $17,000+.

L07-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: Vulnerable road users lack the protective structural metal cage and airbags of passenger cars. They include pedestrians, cyclists, workers, and motorcyclists.

L07-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §552.003, a driver shall yield right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing in a crosswalk when the pedestrian is on the half of the roadway on which the vehicle is traveling or approaching closely.

L07-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Human Resources Code §121.007, an operator approaching a blind person carrying a predominantly white cane or using a guide dog must take necessary precautions to avoid injury and stop.

L07-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §547.008, vehicles designed to operate at a maximum speed of 25 mph or less (such as tractors, farm equipment, and construction machinery) must display an SMV triangular emblem.

L07-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Motorcycles have a narrow profile that makes estimating their speed and distance difficult. Drivers frequently turn left across their path claiming 'I didn't see them'.

L07-T02-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §550.021, an operator involved in an accident resulting in injury or death must immediately stop, determine if aid is required, provide information, and remain at the scene.
L07-T02-Q1.category: DUTY TO STOP AT CRASH SCENE

L07-T02-Q2.statutory_rationale: Fleeing the scene of a fatal accident (Hit and Run) is a 2nd-degree felony under TTC §550.021(c)(1)(A), carrying 2 to 20 years imprisonment and fines up to $10,000.

L07-T02-Q3.statutory_rationale: Texas CPRC §74.151 protects persons who in good faith administer emergency care at the scene of an emergency from civil liability for damages, unless their actions are willfully or wantonly negligent.

L07-T02-Q4.statutory_rationale: TTC §550.023 requires providing name, address, vehicle registration number, showing driver license upon request, and providing liability insurer information.

L07-T02-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §550.024, if you strike an unattended vehicle, you must locate the owner or leave in a conspicuous place a written notice giving your name, address, and statement of circumstances.

L07-T03-Q1.statutory_rationale: TTC §551.101 states that a person operating a bicycle has the rights and duties applicable to a driver operating a motor vehicle, including obeying traffic signs and signals.

L07-T03-Q2.statutory_rationale: Safe passing laws and TDLR driver standards mandate giving bicyclists at least 3 feet of lateral clearance when passing (and 6 feet for commercial vehicles), or changing lanes when safe.

L07-T03-Q3.statutory_rationale: In a turn, trailer wheels follow a shorter path than the cab (off-tracking). A truck turning right may swing wide left first; cutting into the right-hand gap results in being crushed.

L07-T03-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.308, ridden animals have the rights of vehicles. Honking or revving engines can spook a horse, causing it to bolt into traffic or throw its rider.

L07-T03-Q5.statutory_rationale: Light rail trains move rapidly and cannot stop quickly or steer away. Never stop on rail tracks, never attempt to beat a train, and obey transit signals explicitly.

L07-T04-Q1.statutory_rationale: The IPDE process is the core defensive driving strategy: Identify clues in the driving environment, Predict how hazards could develop, Decide what action to take, and Execute smoothly.

L07-T04-Q2.statutory_rationale: Maintaining a visual lead of 12-15 seconds in urban driving and 20-30 seconds on highways allows drivers to detect hazards early and plan actions before an emergency arises.

L07-T04-Q3.statutory_rationale: Defensive driving requires predicting the worst-case scenario: a bouncing ball means a child follows; front wheels turned toward the street mean a parked car may pull out.

L07-T04-Q4.statutory_rationale: Driving in clusters or packs of cars robs you of space cushions. If one driver brakes or loses control, a cascading multi-car collision is almost unavoidable.

L07-T04-Q5.statutory_rationale: Defensive driving is built upon patience, humility, and caution. A defensive driver willingly gives up right-of-way if it prevents a collision, prioritizing safety over pride.

L07-T05-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.413, all occupants in a vehicle equipped with safety belts must be secured, regardless of whether they sit in the front or rear seat.

L07-T05-Q2.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.412 requires child passenger safety seat systems for children younger than 8 years old, unless the child is taller than 4 feet 9 inches (57 inches).

L07-T05-Q3.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.414 makes it a misdemeanor to operate an open-bed pickup truck or open trailer with a passenger under 18 years old in the bed (with narrow agricultural/parade exceptions).

L07-T05-Q4.statutory_rationale: TPC §22.10 makes it a Class C misdemeanor to intentionally or knowingly leave a child younger than 7 unattended in a vehicle for longer than 5 minutes without someone at least 14 years old.

L07-T05-Q5.statutory_rationale: Cars act like greenhouses. Sunlight heats interiors rapidly, rising nearly 20°F in just 10 minutes and reaching fatal levels (110°F-130°F+) even on mild 70°F days. Cracking windows does not help.

L07-T06-Q1.statutory_rationale: Signal your intention, slow down, and steer smoothly to the right shoulder or edge of the road, clear of traffic. Place the vehicle in park and set the parking brake.

L07-T06-Q2.statutory_rationale: Turn on the interior dome light at night so the officer can see inside. Lower the window and keep both hands visibly placed on the steering wheel (at 10 and 2 or 9 and 3).

L07-T06-Q3.statutory_rationale: Always inform the officer where your license and insurance card are located before reaching for them (e.g., 'Officer, my insurance is in the glove compartment; may I reach for it?').

L07-T06-Q4.statutory_rationale: Passengers should remain calm, stay seated inside the car, keep hands in plain view (e.g., on their laps), avoid unannounced movements, and follow officer directions.

L07-T06-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §543.005, signing a traffic citation is merely a promise to appear in court or resolve the citation. It is NOT an admission of guilt. Refusing to sign can result in immediate arrest.

L07-T07-Q1.statutory_rationale: SB 30 was enacted to educate drivers and law enforcement on mutual expectations, rights, and responsibilities during traffic stops, fostering professionalism and preventing tragedies.

L07-T07-Q2.statutory_rationale: During a traffic stop, an officer may ask for driver license, vehicle registration, and insurance. Under U.S. Supreme Court precedent (Mimms), officers may also order driver/passengers to exit for safety.
L07-T07-Q2.statute: TX CODE OF CRIM PROC ART 2.13

L07-T07-Q3.statutory_rationale: Citizens have a First Amendment right to peacefully record police officers performing duties in public, provided they do not obstruct or interfere with the officer's actions.

L07-T07-Q4.statutory_rationale: Never litigate or escalate a dispute on the side of the road. Follow directions during the stop, note the officer's badge number and unit, and file a complaint or commendation afterward.

L07-T07-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under the DPS 7-Step Violator Contact method, troopers greet the driver, state their name/department, explain the reason for the stop, request driver credentials, and handle the interaction professionally.

L07-T08-Q1.statutory_rationale: Aggressive driving involves reckless traffic violations (tailgating, speeding, cutting off). Road rage is a violent criminal act—using a vehicle or weapon to threaten or assault another person.

L07-T08-Q2.statutory_rationale: Eye contact, retaliatory gestures, honking, and brake-checking inflame road rage. Avoid eye contact, stay calm, and let the aggressive driver pass safely.

L07-T08-Q3.statutory_rationale: Never drive home or to an isolated spot. Call 911 and drive to a police station, fire department, or crowded public facility with security. Never exit your vehicle.

L07-T08-Q4.statutory_rationale: Driving while furious or distressed impairs judgment as severely as intoxication. Cool off before driving, focus on safety, and remember driving is not a competition.

L07-T08-Q5.statutory_rationale: Call 911 (hands-free or passenger) and report location (highway and mile marker/cross street), travel direction, vehicle description, license plate if possible, and specific actions.

L07-T09-Q1.statutory_rationale: Safety chains must be crossed under the tongue of the hitch. Crossing forms a cradle that catches the trailer tongue if it drops, preventing it from digging into the road.

L07-T09-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §547.382, loads extending 4+ feet beyond the rear must display a red flag (at least 12 inches square) during daylight, or a red light visible from 500 feet at night.

L07-T09-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §725.021, a vehicle transporting loose materials must have the load completely covered with a canvas or tarp tightly secured to prevent spillage onto highways.

L07-T09-Q4.statutory_rationale: Towing adds substantial momentum, greatly increasing stopping distances. High speeds can cause dangerous trailer sway ('fishtailing') that can jackknife and roll the towing vehicle.

L07-T09-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.409(a), the drawbar or other connection between a towing vehicle and towed vehicle may not exceed 15 feet in length, and must display a white flag if a chain or rope.

L07-T10-Q1.statutory_rationale: Carbon monoxide is an invisible, odorless, tasteless, and non-irritating toxic gas produced by internal combustion engines. Victims become drowsy and unconscious without realizing they are poisoned.

L07-T10-Q2.statutory_rationale: Early symptoms include headache, lightheadedness, nausea, sleepiness, confusion, and weakness. Continued exposure leads to unconsciousness, brain damage, and fatal asphyxiation.

L07-T10-Q3.statutory_rationale: Even with garage doors open, deadly carbon monoxide builds up within minutes and easily seeps into adjacent house living areas. Always back out into the open driveway first.

L07-T10-Q4.statutory_rationale: If the tailpipe is buried or blocked by snow, mud, or water, exhaust gas backs up and penetrates directly into the passenger cabin, causing fatal poisoning in minutes.

L07-T10-Q5.statutory_rationale: Air flowing over a moving car creates a low-pressure vacuum pocket behind the vehicle. An open tailgate sucks exhaust fumes back into the passenger compartment.

L07-T11-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.157, drivers must vacate the lane closest to stopped emergency vehicles, or slow to a speed 20 mph less than the posted speed limit (or 5 mph if limit is < 25 mph).

L07-T11-Q2.statutory_rationale: The Move Over Act covers police, emergency medical, fire, tow trucks, TxDOT maintenance vehicles, utility service vehicles, and recently expanded to any stationary vehicle with hazard lights.

L07-T11-Q3.statutory_rationale: A standard violation carries fines up to $200 (or $500-$1,250 on second offense). However, if the violation results in bodily injury, it is a Class A misdemeanor (up to $4,000 fine / 1 yr jail).

L07-T11-Q4.statutory_rationale: Officers, paramedics, tow operators, and road workers are frequently struck and killed by inattentive drivers clipping them on highway shoulders. The law creates a mandatory safety buffer.

L07-T11-Q5.statutory_rationale: If driving on a highway with two or more lanes in the same direction, your first statutory duty is to move out of the lane closest to the emergency vehicle if lane change is safe.

L07-T12-Q1.statutory_rationale: Pilot vehicles warn traffic that an oversize load is traveling on the road. The rig may occupy more than one lane, have limited braking ability, and make exceptionally wide turns.

L07-T12-Q2.statutory_rationale: Trucks cannot turn right from a tight lane without their trailer hitting the curb. Drivers swing wide left first. Squeezing into the open right space places you directly in the trailer's crush path.

L07-T12-Q3.statutory_rationale: Pass smoothly on the left without lingering in the truck's blind spots. Do not cut in front; wait until you can see both headlights of the truck in your inside rearview mirror.

L07-T12-Q4.statutory_rationale: An 80,000-lb truck descending a hill accumulates massive kinetic energy. If brakes overheat, 'brake fade' occurs, leading to runaway truck scenarios. Never pull in front of a truck on hills.

L07-T12-Q5.statutory_rationale: Runaway truck ramps use deep gravel or upward slopes to safely arrest out-of-control trucks that experienced brake failure. Never park or stop on or near a runaway truck ramp.

L07-T13-Q1.statutory_rationale: The Texas Driving with Disabilities Program was created to alert law enforcement to communication impediments before approaching a vehicle, reducing misunderstandings during stops.

L07-T13-Q2.statutory_rationale: Individuals with autism or PTSD may exhibit anxiety, avoid eye contact, freeze, or take longer to answer questions. Unaware officers could misinterpret these behaviors as intoxication or evasion.

L07-T13-Q3.statutory_rationale: Participation is completely voluntary. The driver or vehicle owner has complete discretion over whether to participate and have the indicator added to their license or registration.

L07-T13-Q4.statutory_rationale: The program is a joint effort between the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV), the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS), and licensed medical practitioners.

L07-T13-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under Texas law, information submitted for the program is confidential, exempt from public disclosure under the Public Information Act, and accessible only to authorized law enforcement.

L07-T14-Q1.statutory_rationale: Participation requires an application form certified and signed by a licensed physician or health professional verifying the applicant's communication impediment diagnosis.

L07-T14-Q2.statutory_rationale: Drivers can choose either or both options: registering their vehicle's license plate in the TLETS database through TxDMV, and/or adding the notation to their driver license through DPS.

L07-T14-Q3.statutory_rationale: TxDMV charges no additional fee to include the communication impediment indicator on your vehicle registration. Standard registration fees apply.

L07-T14-Q4.statutory_rationale: Once enrolled, the communication impediment notation remains linked with the vehicle's registration record across standard renewals until the owner requests removal.

L07-T14-Q5.statutory_rationale: Yes! A parent or guardian who owns the vehicle can enroll if a person with a communication impediment is regularly transported in the vehicle, preparing officers who run the plate.

L07-T15-Q1.statutory_rationale: Qualifying diagnoses include Autism Spectrum Disorder, Down Syndrome, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Asperger Syndrome, mutism, brain injuries, and severe speech disorders.

L07-T15-Q2.statutory_rationale: When officers know a driver is deaf or hard of hearing, they avoid shouting, face the driver directly for lip reading, and utilize written notes or visual gestures.

L07-T15-Q3.statutory_rationale: High-intensity flashing strobes, sirens, and sudden loud commands can cause autistic drivers to experience acute sensory overload, leading to agitation, shut-down, or panic.

L07-T15-Q4.statutory_rationale: A traffic stop can trigger intense fight-or-flight reactions in individuals with PTSD. Knowing this allows the officer to approach calmly and speak clearly without sudden confrontational tactics.

L07-T15-Q5.statutory_rationale: The medical professional signing the form must be licensed by the state (physician, psychologist, or speech-language pathologist) and verify that the condition impedes communication.

L07-T16-Q1.statutory_rationale: Physical disabilities relate to mobility limitations (requiring wheelchairs, crutches, oxygen, or limited walking). They qualify for blue disability parking placards (TTC Chapter 681).

L07-T16-Q2.statutory_rationale: Communication impediments affect speech, hearing, or social communication under stress. Crucially, a communication impediment alone does NOT grant disabled parking privileges.

L07-T16-Q3.statutory_rationale: A driver with both physical mobility limitations and a neurological/speech communication impediment can hold both a disabled parking placard and the TLETS communication indicator.

L07-T16-Q4.statutory_rationale: TTC §681.011 makes parking in a disabled space without a legitimate placard/plate a misdemeanor punishable by fines up to $500-$750 for first offense, escalating to $1,250 + community service.

L07-T16-Q5.statutory_rationale: The striped area adjacent to accessible parking spaces is an access aisle. Blocking it prevents individuals with wheelchair vans from deploying ramps, trapping them in or out of their cars.

L07-T17-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §521.125, the DPS shall print a communication impediment notation on the license of an eligible applicant upon request, maintaining privacy while alerting officials.

L07-T17-Q2.statutory_rationale: To protect individual privacy and prevent stigma, the card simply notes 'Communication Impediment'. It does NOT disclose whether the cause is autism, PTSD, mutism, or hearing loss.

L07-T17-Q3.statutory_rationale: When handed the license, the officer immediately recognizes the notation, allowing them to adjust tone, provide clear step-by-step instructions, and avoid misinterpreting anxiety.

L07-T17-Q4.statutory_rationale: Deaf drivers often have a specific restriction (such as Restriction Code 8 or hearing impairment endorsement / outside rearview mirror requirement) noted on their Texas license.

L07-T17-Q5.statutory_rationale: Because the program is voluntary, an individual can request removal of the indicator from their driver license record at any time by submitting an application for a duplicate/corrected license.

L07-T18-Q1.statutory_rationale: Form VTR-214 is the official TxDMV 'Application for Communication Impediment with Law Enforcement' form used to tie the indicator to the vehicle's license plate in TLETS.

L07-T18-Q2.statutory_rationale: TLETS is the statewide computer network law enforcement uses. When an officer runs a license plate prior to exiting the patrol car, TLETS immediately displays the communication impediment alert.

L07-T18-Q3.statutory_rationale: If only on the license, the officer doesn't know until after approaching the window. TLETS informs the officer before they walk up, allowing them to approach calmly with full understanding.

L07-T18-Q4.statutory_rationale: Form VTR-214, certified by a doctor, is submitted to the local County Tax Assessor-Collector's office during registration or mailed directly to TxDMV Vehicle Titles and Registration.

L07-T18-Q5.statutory_rationale: For privacy and safety, there is NO external symbol, decal, or marking on the physical license plate. The indicator is strictly electronic, visible only to law enforcement in the secure TLETS database.

L08-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: Over 90-94% of all motor vehicle crashes are caused by preventable driver errors—including speeding, distraction, intoxication, failure to yield, and following too closely.

L08-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: TxDOT estimates traffic crashes cost Texans tens of billions of dollars each year in medical treatment, emergency response, lost wages, insurance rate increases, and property destruction.

L08-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: Accidents imply random fate that cannot be avoided. Traffic safety experts use 'crash' or 'collision' because almost all collisions result from specific choices that could have been prevented.

L08-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: Space gives you time to react. Preserving an adequate following cushion (3-4+ seconds) and maintaining an open space on at least one side ensures an escape route when emergencies occur.

L08-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Driving is a social, cooperative activity. A driver who follows laws, stays sober, and eliminates distractions protects the lives of innocent pedestrians, children, and fellow road users.

L08-T02-Q1.statutory_rationale: 'Turn Around, Don't Drown' is the national rule. Water depth and road stability cannot be judged from the driver seat; roads can wash out underneath without visible surface evidence.

L08-T02-Q2.statutory_rationale: Pull completely off the roadway, turn off all lights (including brake lights so trailing drivers don't follow your lights into you), set the parking brake, and remain buckled inside.

L08-T02-Q3.statutory_rationale: High-profile vehicles (trailers, RVs, commercial box trucks) have large surface areas that act like sails in crosswinds. Sudden gusts can push them across lanes or overturn them.

L08-T02-Q4.statutory_rationale: Dirty windshields magnify glare dramatically. Clean windshields inside and out, use polarized sunglasses and visors, slow down, and leave extra following distance.

L08-T02-Q5.statutory_rationale: Never use high beams in fog. Light reflects off water droplets straight back into your eyes, causing blinding glare. Low beams direct light downward onto the road surface.

L08-T03-Q1.statutory_rationale: Underinflated tires flex excessively, generating dangerous heat on hot Texas highways that weakens tire belts and causes sudden, catastrophic tire blowouts and rollovers.

L08-T03-Q2.statutory_rationale: The correct pressure is on the driver's doorjamb sticker or owner's manual. The number stamped on the tire sidewall is the MAXIMUM pressure the tire can hold, NOT recommended driving pressure.

L08-T03-Q3.statutory_rationale: A soft or sinking pedal indicates air in the lines, worn master cylinder, or leaking brake fluid. Driving with this symptom is extremely dangerous; immediate mechanical repair is required.

L08-T03-Q4.statutory_rationale: Texas heat and UV rays dry out and crack rubber wiper blades quickly. Replace blades every 6 to 12 months or as soon as they streak, smear, or skip across the windshield.

L08-T03-Q5.statutory_rationale: All factory lights must work: 2 headlights (high/low beam), 2 taillights, 2-3 brake lights, turn signals front and rear, hazard flashers, and white license plate lamp.

L08-T04-Q1.statutory_rationale: The three recognized categories are: Visual (looking away), Manual (removing hands from controls), and Cognitive (mental focus wandering from the driving task).

L08-T04-Q2.statutory_rationale: The brain cannot fully process two cognitively demanding tasks at once. Even with hands on the wheel, phone conversations divert mental attention, causing 'inattention blindness'.

L08-T04-Q3.statutory_rationale: A lap pet can wedge under brake pedals, block steering movements, and in a collision, will be crushed by deploying airbags or launched as a lethal projectile into passengers.

L08-T04-Q4.statutory_rationale: Entering addresses while driving combines visual, manual, and cognitive distractions. Set your destination before shifting into drive, or pull into a safe parking lot to adjust.

L08-T04-Q5.statutory_rationale: Studies show crash risk multiplies with each additional young passenger. Rowdy conversations, loud music, and peer pressure to speed severely divert attention from the road.

L08-T05-Q1.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.420 makes racing on a highway a Class B misdemeanor on 1st offense (up to $2,000 fine / 180 days jail), escalating to Class A or 3rd/2nd-degree felony if injury or death occurs.

L08-T05-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under Texas law, peace officers seize and impound vehicles used in illegal street racing or speed contests, requiring owners to pay significant towing and daily storage fees.

L08-T05-Q3.statutory_rationale: Texas statutes penalize not just drivers, but also individuals who organize, facilitate, or knowingly spectate at street takeovers and illegal speed contests.

L08-T05-Q4.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.420(h), if street racing results in the death of a person, the offense is elevated to a 2nd-degree felony, carrying 2 to 20 years in prison and up to $10,000 in fines.

L08-T05-Q5.statutory_rationale: Impact force is governed by kinetic energy (E = 1/2 m v^2). A crash at 60 mph has four times the destructive force of a crash at 30 mph, easily crushing vehicle structural safety cells.

L08-T06-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.251, an operator approaching a railroad crossing must stop not closer than 15 feet or farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail when warning signals flash or a train approaches.

L08-T06-Q2.statutory_rationale: The blue Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign on the signal post lists the railroad's 24/7 dispatch phone number and the crossing's unique USDOT inventory number to stop trains.

L08-T06-Q3.statutory_rationale: Exit immediately! Run at a 45-degree angle TOWARD the approaching train and away from tracks. When the train impacts the car, debris is thrown forward in the train's direction of travel.

L08-T06-Q4.statutory_rationale: A 100-car freight train weighing 12 million pounds traveling at 55 mph requires at least a mile (over 5,280 feet) to stop. The train CANNOT stop in time to avoid an object on the tracks.

L08-T06-Q5.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.251(a)(5), it is strictly illegal to drive around, under, or through a crossing gate while it is closed or being opened/closed. Never assume a gate is broken.

L08-T07-Q1.statutory_rationale: Overdriving headlights means driving so fast that you cannot stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights. By the time you spot an obstacle, a crash is mathematically unavoidable.

L08-T07-Q2.statutory_rationale: Standard low beams illuminate roughly 150-200 feet ahead. High beams illuminate about 350-400 feet. At 65 mph, total stopping distance exceeds 300 feet, making low beams easy to overdrive.

L08-T07-Q3.statutory_rationale: Do not look directly at oncoming lights; this causes temporary retinal blindness. Look down toward the right-hand edge of your lane or the white fog line to guide your path safely.

L08-T07-Q4.statutory_rationale: During dusk and dawn, the sky still has ambient light but shadows lengthen and road contrast drops drastically. Human eyes struggle to adapt to the transition, obscuring pedestrians and hazards.

L08-T07-Q5.statutory_rationale: Despite carrying only 25% of total traffic, nighttime driving accounts for nearly half of all fatal crashes. Reduced visibility, fatigue, intoxication, and higher speeds multiply risk by three.

L08-T08-Q1.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.4251 bans reading, writing, or sending electronic messages (texts, emails, DMs) while operating a motor vehicle on Texas roadways unless stopped outside traffic lanes.

L08-T08-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.425, using any handheld wireless communication device in an active school crossing zone is strictly prohibited unless stopped or in an emergency.

L08-T08-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.424, drivers under 18 years of age are completely prohibited from using any wireless communication device (including hands-free/Bluetooth) except for emergencies.

L08-T08-Q4.statutory_rationale: A first texting conviction carries a fine between $25 and $99. Repeat offenses carry fines from $100 to $200. If texting causes serious injury or death, it becomes a Class A misdemeanor.

L08-T08-Q5.statutory_rationale: At 55 mph, a car travels roughly 80.7 feet per second. Looking away for 5 seconds means traveling over 400 feet—the entire length of a football field—with your eyes completely closed.

L08-T09-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §550.022 ('Steer It & Clear It'), if a crash occurs on a main lane of a freeway and vehicles can be driven safely, operators MUST move vehicles off the freeway to restore traffic flow.

L08-T09-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §550.062, an officer must submit an official crash report (Form CR-3) if the accident resulted in injury, death, or apparent property damage of $1,000 or more to any one person.

L08-T09-Q3.statutory_rationale: The official report is Form CR-3 (Texas Peace Officer's Crash Report), transmitted to TxDOT's CRIS (Crash Records Information System) and accessible to insurers and involved parties.

L08-T09-Q4.statutory_rationale: Safety is paramount: check for injuries, prevent secondary crashes by turning on hazards, call 911, and ensure occupants are out of dangerous traffic flow before exchanging details.

L08-T09-Q5.statutory_rationale: Policy contracts require timely notification. Promptly reporting ensures your insurer can collect evidence, contact other parties, and defend you against fraudulent or inflated claims.

L08-T10-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Education Code §1001.1021 (Julia Wells Act), all driver education courses must include instruction on human trafficking awareness, prevention, and reporting protocols.

L08-T10-Q2.statutory_rationale: Indicators include: fear of authority, signs of physical abuse, lack of control over money/ID, coached or rehearsed responses, and being constantly monitored by a controlling person.

L08-T10-Q3.statutory_rationale: The National Human Trafficking Hotline is 1-888-373-7888. It is confidential, toll-free, multilingual, and operates 24/7. Citizens can also text 'HELP' or 'INFO' to 233733 (BeFree).

L08-T10-Q4.statutory_rationale: NEVER attempt to confront traffickers or rescue victims yourself. Traffickers can be armed and dangerous, and confronting them endangers the victim. Call 911 or the hotline immediately.

L08-T10-Q5.statutory_rationale: Trafficking of persons under TPC §20A.02 is a 2nd or 1st-degree felony (escalating to mandatory 25 years to life if child victims or serious injury/death are involved).

L09-T01-Q1.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.151, when two vehicles approach an intersection from different highways at approximately the same time, the operator of the vehicle on the left shall yield to the vehicle on the right.

L09-T01-Q2.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.157, drivers must vacate the lane or slow to 20 mph below the posted speed limit (or slow to 5 mph if the posted limit is under 25 mph).

L09-T01-Q3.statutory_rationale: Under TPC §49.01(2)(B), 0.08 BAC is the statutory per se intoxication threshold in Texas, regardless of whether behavioral impairment is visibly apparent.

L09-T01-Q4.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.412 mandates child safety seat systems for all children younger than 8 years old unless they have reached 4 feet 9 inches (57 inches) in height.

L09-T01-Q5.statutory_rationale: Enrolling via Form VTR-214 places a communication impediment indicator in TLETS. When an officer runs the plate before approaching, they are alerted to communicate with patience and clarity.
